question_text: The slide shows a timeline of female trainers at the Kentucky Derby from 1937 (Mary Hirsch) through 2026 (Cherie DeVaux, horse Golden Tempo, finishing 1st, highlighted). The question asks: What was finally achieved on May 2nd this year, after 90 years since its first instance?
answer_text: The first-ever win by a woman trainer at the Kentucky Derby: Cherie DeVaux became the first female trainer to win the Kentucky Derby, with her horse Golden Tempo, 90 years after Mary Hirsch became the first licensed female trainer to compete in the race (1937).

question_text: Post the main action for which we know him for, X's life took some incredibly diverse paths. He became a certified member of Mensa. He used the money he made from the Hollywood movie rights to go to law school at the University of Pennsylvania, graduated at age 51, and became a communications lawyer in Washington D.C. Later in life, he even worked for the Pentagon as a special assistant representing the Defense Department on POW/MIA (Prisoner of War/Missing in Action) issues, responsible for outreach to veterans and their families. He travelled widely and gave frequent media interviews and public appearances. This led to his becoming a popular after-dinner speaker and lecturer. He appeared as a guest on talk shows such as NBC Radio's Jim Bohanan Show; NBC TV's Today show; Fox News's Hannity & Colmes, ABC's Bill Maher; and the PBS series Freedom Speaks. Who is X?
answer_text: Adrian Cronauer, the real-life U.S. Armed Forces radio DJ in Vietnam, as portrayed by Robin Williams in the movie Good Morning, Vietnam!

question_text: This is a scene from Breathe, a 2017 biopic directed by Andy Serkis in his directorial debut. It is based on the true story of Robin X, one of the UK's longest-living Ys (shown in a cricket scene from the film). X was a British noble family of Anglo-Norman origin that may remind you of a renowned experimental and theoretical chemist noted for his discovery of hydrogen. Y is a portmanteau, created by combining two words, representing individuals who use breathing tech to venture out and navigate their universe. Identify X and Y.
answer_text: X = Cavendish (the family name of Robin Cavendish, and also the surname of chemist Henry Cavendish, discoverer of hydrogen). Y = Responaut (a portmanteau of 'respirator' and 'astronaut', referring to a person who uses a wheelchair respirator to live an active life).

question_text: The connection between BoJack Horseman and X centres on the most famous piece of art featured in the Netflix series: a parody of X's iconic 1972 painting. Hung prominently on the back wall of BoJack's office, the show's version anthropomorphizes the original piece by replacing human subjects with horses. In the parody, a horse wearing a white Speedo swims underwater while another horse stands at the edge of the pool looking down. Just as X's pool series explored the hollow, artificial nature of the luxurious California lifestyle, the painting mirrors BoJack's isolation amid Hollywood opulence. In the real art world, X's original masterpiece made history in 2018 when it was auctioned for $90.3 million, briefly holding the record for the most expensive painting sold by a living artist. X passed away 3 weeks ago on 11th June at 88. Who is X?
answer_text: David Hockney, the British artist, whose 1972 painting 'Portrait of an Artist (Pool with Two Figures)' was parodied in BoJack Horseman and sold for $90.3 million in 2018.

question_text: Cartas Telepáticas (Telepathic Letters) is a 2024 film, created with AI images, that explores the invisible links between two iconic authors X and Y. X and Y were exact contemporaries who never met, yet they shared a profound literary kinship. Both were pioneers of the 20th century avant-garde obsessed with the fragmentation of identity, existential dread, and the profound unreliability of reality. X, one of the most significant literary figures of the 20th century and one of the greatest poets in Portuguese literature, invented the term 'heteronyms' to escape cosmic dread, dying obscure before becoming a modern cult icon. Y, an American writer of weird, horror, fantasy, and science fiction, projected that exact same existential dread, and just like X, used various pseudonyms, sought escape from a disappointing reality through a vast literary 'Dream-Cycle'. Identify X and Y.
answer_text: X = Fernando Pessoa; Y = H.P. Lovecraft.

question_text: X was an Indian revolutionary who participated in the Indian independence movement. She was leading one of the five batches of volunteers (of the Vidyut Bahini), constituted by the Samar Parishad (War Council), at Tamluk to capture the Tamluk Police Station on 29 September 1942, when she was shot dead by the British Indian police in front of the police station, becoming the first 'Quit India' movement martyr in Midnapore. She was a staunch Gandhian and was fondly called Gandhi buri, Bengali for 'old lady Gandhi'. Post India's independence in 1947, numerous schools, colonies, and streets, including a long stretch in Kolkata, were named after X. The first statue of a woman put up in Kolkata in independent India was X's, in 1977. Who is X?
answer_text: Matangini Hazra.

question_text: What is being talked about? Three picture clues are given: a photo of a bearded man (representing brothers Tom and John's friend, X Newball, with an extra 'e' added to signify the concept of belief or credit); the Olympia Beer logo (inspired by a television commercial for Olympia Beer that used the phrase 'X Y'); and an image of Frankenstein's monster (added to represent the renewed commitment after a hiatus; also the title of a Stephen King novel inspired by Mary Shelley's Frankenstein). What is being discussed?
answer_text: The naming of the band Creedence Clearwater Revival: 'Creedence' from their friend Credence Newball (respelled with an extra 'e'), 'Clearwater' from an Olympia Beer commercial phrase, and 'Revival' marking the band's renewed commitment (and echoing Stephen King's novel Revival).

question_text: X was Y's lucky number, so when Ernest Beaux presented Y with 10 samples for their first creation together, Y picked number X, as it was Y's favorite numeral. It is now considered the most famous ___ in the world, and the number X recurs throughout Y's creations. At the age of twelve, Y was handed over to the care of nuns, and for the next six years spent a stark, disciplined existence in a convent orphanage, Aubazine, founded by 12th century Cistercians in the Corrèze department of south-west France. From earliest days there, the number X had potent associations for Y. For Y, the number was especially esteemed as signifying the pure embodiment of a thing, its spirit, its mystic meaning. The paths that led Y to the cathedral for daily prayers were laid out in circular patterns repeating the number X. Identify X and Y.
answer_text: X = 5 (the number); Y = Coco Chanel. Together: Chanel No. 5, the famous perfume created with perfumer Ernest Beaux.

question_text: Connect. Five images are shown: a map of the United States with the Mississippi River highlighted in red; a classical colonnaded memorial/pavilion on a waterfront (resembling a monument at Plymouth, Massachusetts); a domed gazebo labelled 'Columbian Spring' on a university campus; the seal of Susquehanna University, Selinsgrove, Pennsylvania; and a headshot of actor Matthew Perry.

question_text: AgniKul Cosmos Private Limited is a private Indian aerospace manufacturer and commercial launch service provider based in the National Centre for Combustion Research and Development (NCCRD) of IIT Madras, Chennai. The start-up aims to develop and launch its own small-lift launch vehicle such as the Agnibaan, capable of placing 100 kg payload into a 700 km orbit. The first suborbital test vehicle was successfully launched on 30 May 2024. This mission achieved several notable milestones like: use of Linux-based flight computers, an Ethernet-based architecture, a first for Indian rockets; India's first semi-cryo engine launch; and India's first launch from a private launch pad. However, the biggest first of these all was it being the world's first space flight with a X. Through this achievement, the company now claims they can reduce the traditional manufacturing timeline by nearly 97%. What is X?
answer_text: A single-piece, fully 3D-printed rocket engine (the world's first space flight using a single-piece 3D printed engine).

question_text: The Livraria Lello & Irmão, commonly known in English as the Lello Bookshop, is a bookshop located in the civil parish of Cedofeita, Santo Ildefonso, Sé, Miragaia, São Nicolau e Vitória, in the northern Portuguese municipality of Porto. Along with Bertrand, it is one of the oldest bookstores in Portugal and frequently rated among the greatest bookstores in the world. Recently, the library has introduced a section of banned and censored books called 'The Manifesto Library'. Controversial books like Margaret Atwood's The Handmaid's Tale, Reginald Dwayne Betts' Felon, alongside selected works from Salman Rushdie and Olga Tokarczuk are available. Which famous patron of literature has launched this section in partnership with Lello?
answer_text: Dua Lipa, through her Service95 Book Club.

question_text: The literal meaning of this word X derives from the Spanish verb for conjoining or conjugation. In Italy, this word is the civil executive of regions and municipalities (comune). In Spain, the term refers to various historical and current governing institutions of a particular territory or occasion, like under Habsburg rule, it was an administrative body ruled in personal union with the Spanish Habsburgs. In England, the earliest example of this term was with New Model Trade Unions (NMTU), that were a variety of Trade Unions prominent in the 1850s and 1860s in the UK. In English, the term, even when used alone, also can refer to a military state, the government of an authoritarian state run by high-ranking officers of a military. What is this word, which in Indian context, can be interpreted, at least as a heteronym, a completely opposite, anti-authoritarian noun?
answer_text: Junta. In the Indian/Hindi context, the similarly-sounding word 'Janata' (जनता) means 'the people' (as in Ramdhari Singh Dinkar's famous line, 'Singhasan khali karo ke janta aati hai' - 'Vacate the throne, for the people are coming'), the opposite, anti-authoritarian sense of the authoritarian military 'junta'.

question_text: X was an anti-colonial activist and politician who governed Y as its Prime Minister from 1963 to 1964 and then as its first President from 1964 to his death in 1978. He played a significant role in the transformation of Y from a colony of the British Empire into an independent republic. His government was responsible for numerous massacres of ethnic minorities in Y, particularly ethnic civilians from a neighbouring country. During his presidency, he was lauded as the Father of the Nation, but his rule was criticised as dictatorial, authoritarian, and neocolonial. His son later also became president. As a teenager, X lived with the family of an aunt who had married a local chief, adopting customs and wearing jewellery, including a beaded belt called X* (a homophone of X) in local language. At some point, he took to calling himself X after this garment. A hint to think of X and Y is to think on the lines of Arsene Wenger and Arsenal. Identify X.
answer_text: Jomo Kenyatta, the first Prime Minister and President of Kenya (Y).

question_text: X, the director behind the sports movie Secretariat based on the thoroughbred horse and the war movie We Were Soldiers dramatizing the Battle of Ia Drang, started his film career as a screenwriter. His most famous written work was Y, which was inspired by a trip to ___ to learn more about his roots. While there, he discovered the legend of a local hero sharing the same last name as him. His shared ancestry with the hero is only a report from a cousin in the army who was stationed in Europe. Some years later, as Y became a global sensation and this question arose in the minds of many, he undertook a genealogy test, where he established his ancestors had come to America from ___ in 1660s, and settled in American South. But he couldn't fully establish the ancestry of that hero. When asked in an interview, he said 'It is my understanding that no one knows the names of his immediate descendants, so direct ancestry might be impossible to prove. But I am absolutely convinced he is an ancestor and no one can prove that he is not.' Identify X and Y.
answer_text: X = Randall Wallace, the director/screenwriter; Y = Braveheart, inspired by his trip to Scotland and the legend of William Wallace.

question_text: There is a remarkable similarity in the fortunes of these two teams, but not entirely without a connection. X's coach A was flying high after winning the World Cup in 1978 in Argentina, having defeated the Netherlands 3-2 in the final and earning applause from all corners. X had mastered the double attack strategy through which their seven-man attack was capable of pouncing on the opponent's goal from both flanks. Resultantly, X dominated the entire tournament scoring 35 goals, the highest by any team in a World Cup, while conceding only 4 goals in 575 minutes of play. The GD of +31 is still a world record. On the other hand, Y had a charismatic coach B who was spellbound by X's gameplay. Coincidentally, both X and Y teams were staying in the same hotel in Buenos Aires. B paid a surprise visit to A where he took some notes. A few weeks later, Y also ended up beating the Netherlands 3-1 in another final, staging an uncanny repeat of X's feat. Identify X, Y, A and B.
answer_text: X = Pakistan men's hockey team, A = Abdul Waheed Khan (coach); Y = Argentina men's football team, B = César Luis Menotti (coach). Both teams beat the Netherlands in their respective 1978 World Cup finals (hockey and football).

question_text: Daphne was a Naiad Nymph in Greek Mythology. She was famous for being incredibly beautiful and for catching the eye of god Apollo. However, Daphne was determined to remain unmarried and untouched by a man for the rest of her life. Meanwhile, Apollo had been mocking the God of Love, Eros. In retaliation, Eros fired two arrows: a golden arrow that struck Apollo and made him madly in love with Daphne, and a lead arrow that made Daphne hate Apollo. Because of his repeated advances, Daphne turned to the river god, Peneus, and pleaded to him to free her from Apollo. In response, Peneus used metamorphosis to turn Daphne into a X, thus leaving Apollo's love unrequited. Heartbroken, Apollo used his powers of eternal youth to immortalize Daphne's X, and vowed to keep it close to him forever - leading to a ritual followed to this day in the world of sports, academia, entertainment, among others. What are we talking about?
answer_text: A laurel tree. Apollo wore a laurel wreath on his head to immortalize Daphne, giving rise to the ritual of wearing laurel wreaths in graduation ceremonies, sports victories, and other honours.

question_text: Alyssa Carson is a 25-year-old American social media influencer known for her unrelenting ambition from a young age to ___. She uses the social media branding X-Blueberry, but X has denied any association or affiliation. She has been working on her ambition for years now since a very young age, in the process becoming the only person to attend every X event including those in Turkey and Canada. To fuel this passion, she did her graduation from Florida Tech, a small, private research university where she spent time in the lab studying microbes, specifically plant-growth-promoting bacteria, that could help grow food without essentials of photosynthesis. Because of her dedication and efforts, she has become a brand ambassador of products like specific-use items designed by Horizn Studios and Final Frontier Design's products for X's Canadian counterpart. What is Alyssa Carson's life goal (and what is X)?
answer_text: Her life goal is to become the first person to go to Mars. X is NASA (she uses the social media handle 'NasaBlueberry', though NASA has not endorsed or affiliated with her).

question_text: In June 2026, as per Variety magazine, X became the latest entrant to the prestigious EGOT list when 'Schmigadoon!' won a Tony Award. It is a stage musical that has been adapted from a 2021 musical comedy TV show. The plot follows two New York City doctors, Melissa Gimble and Josh Skinner, struggling with their romantic relationship, who find themselves trapped in the titular magical town like the setting of a Golden Age musical. In the process, X became the fastest to win all 4 awards, with multiple Emmy wins (latest in 2023), an Oscar for CODA (2021), and a Grammy for 'Bad as I Used to Be' from F1 the movie (2026) previously. Identify X.
answer_text: Apple (Apple Studios/Apple Original Films), which became the first studio to achieve a 'Studio EGOT' through Schmigadoon! (Netflix had already achieved a form of this in 2024). The 'fastest' claim is a misdirect for an individual EGOT - songwriters Benj Pasek and Justin Paul still hold the record for fastest individual EGOT at 7 years 7 months.
